title: Topic 71 | Current, voltage and resistance in an AC circuit

questions.text: A resistor, a capacitor and a coil are connected in series to an AC source. The amplitude of the voltage oscillations is $4$ V across the resistor, $6$ V across the capacitor and $3$ V across the coil. What is the amplitude of the voltage oscillations across the source terminals (in volts)?

An inductor, a capacitor and a resistor are connected in series to an AC circuit. The voltages across the inductor, the capacitor and the resistor are $30$ V, $24$ V and $8$ V, respectively. What is the total voltage in the circuit (V)?

A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series to an AC circuit. A voltmeter connected across the resistor reads $60$ V, and a voltmeter connected across the capacitor reads $80$ V. What is the total voltage in the mains (V)?
In the circuit shown in the figure, the voltages are $U_L=80$ V and $U_C=60$ V. What is $U$ (in volts)?

An inductor and a capacitor are connected in series to an AC circuit. A voltmeter connected across the inductor reads $400$ V, and a voltmeter connected across the capacitor reads $180$ V. What is the total voltage in the mains (V)?

A resistance and an inductor are connected in series to an AC source. The potential difference between points AB is $40$ V and between points BC is $30$ V. What is the potential difference between points AC (V)?
A circuit consists of a $24~\Omega$ resistance, a $30~\Omega$ capacitive reactance and a $30~\Omega$ inductive reactance connected in series. Find the impedance of the circuit ($\Omega$).

A resistor of resistance $70~\Omega$, a capacitor of reactance $6~\Omega$ and an inductor of reactance $30~\Omega$ are connected in series to an AC circuit. What is the impedance of the circuit ($\Omega$)?

In an AC circuit with an angular frequency of $1000$ rad/s, an inductor of inductance $2$ H and a capacitor of capacitance $1~\mu$F are connected in series. Find the impedance of the circuit (k$\Omega$).

An inductor of inductance $31.4$ H and a capacitor of capacitance $314$ nF are connected in series to a circuit. If the AC frequency is $50$ Hz, what is the impedance of the circuit ($\Omega$)? Neglect the resistance of the connecting wires. $\pi^2\approx10$.

A resistance of $8~\text{k}\Omega$ and an inductor of inductance $20$ H are connected in series to an AC source. If the frequency of the alternating current is $50$ Hz, find the impedance of the circuit (k$\Omega$). $\pi=3$.
The impedance of the AC circuit shown below is $Z=3\sqrt5~\Omega$. If $R_1=12~\Omega$, $X_L=10~\Omega$ and $X_C=4~\Omega$, what is $R_2$ ($\Omega$)?

A capacitor of capacitance $100~\mu$F, an inductor of inductance $200$ mH and a rheostat of resistance $60~\Omega$ are connected in series. The current in the circuit varies as $i=8\sin100t$. What is the impedance of the circuit ($\Omega$)?

In an AC circuit with an angular frequency of $300$ rad/s, a resistor of resistance $4~\Omega$ and an inductor of inductance $10$ mH are connected in series. If the current amplitude in the circuit is $50$ A, what is the amplitude of the voltage across the circuit (V)?
The resistance of an AC circuit is $16~\Omega$ and its reactance is $12~\Omega$. What is the power factor of the circuit?
The resistance of a circuit is $7~\Omega$ and its reactance is $24~\Omega$. What is the power factor of the circuit?

In an AC circuit with an angular frequency of $10^3$ rad/s, a resistor of resistance $15~\Omega$ and an inductor of inductance $0.02$ H are connected in series. If the amplitude of the total voltage in the circuit is $1$ kV, what is the current amplitude (A)?

A capacitor of reactance $10~\Omega$ and an inductor of reactance $20~\Omega$ are connected in series to an AC circuit. If the rms (effective) value of the current is $2$ A, what is the rms value of the voltage across the circuit (V)?

In an AC circuit with an angular frequency of $10^4$ rad/s, a resistor of resistance $100~\Omega$ and a capacitor of capacitance $1~\mu$F are connected in series. The amplitude of the applied voltage is $300$ V. What is the amplitude of the current in the circuit (A)?

A resistor of resistance $10~\Omega$, an inductor of reactance $20~\Omega$ and a capacitor of reactance $30~\Omega$ are connected in series to an AC circuit. If the amplitude of the AC voltage is $200$ V, what is the current amplitude (A)?
A circuit consists of a $9~\Omega$ resistance and a $12~\Omega$ inductive reactance connected in series. What is the cosine of the phase shift between the current and voltage oscillations?
A circuit consists of an $18~\Omega$ resistance and a $24~\Omega$ capacitive reactance connected in series. Find the cosine of the phase shift between the current and voltage oscillations.
Find the rms value of the current in this electric circuit (A).
Find the power factor ($\cos\Delta\varphi$) of this electric circuit.
The two electric circuits shown in the figures have the same power factor. Find the ratio of the rms currents in the two circuits, $I_1/I_2$.

The voltage in this electric circuit varies as
$u=U\sin\omega t$,
and the current varies as
$i=I\sin\left(\omega t-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$.
Find the inductive reactance ($X_L$) in the circuit ($\Omega$).

The voltage in this electric circuit varies as
$u=U\sin\omega t$,
and the current varies as
$i=10\sqrt2\sin\left(50t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$.
Find the rms value of the voltage in the circuit (V). $[u]=$volt, $[i]=$ampere.
Find the rms value of the current in this electric circuit (A).
The impedance vector of the circuit below is shown in Figure 2. Find the rms value of the voltage drop across the capacitor (V). $\sin53^0=0.8$, $\cos53^0=0.6$.
A resistor, an inductor and a capacitor are connected in series. What is the impedance of the circuit at resonance?
answers: many times less than the resistance.

questions.text: In an AC circuit, an inductor, a capacitor and a resistance are connected in series. At resonance, what is the phase difference between the current and the voltage?
answers: the current leads the voltage by $\pi/2$.
the current lags behind the voltage by $\pi/2$.
the current leads the voltage by $\pi$.
the current lags behind the voltage by $\pi$.

questions.text: In an AC circuit, an inductor of inductance $50$ mH and a capacitor of capacitance $20~\mu$F are connected in series. Find the angular frequency (rad/s) at which resonance occurs in the circuit.

An AC circuit of frequency $100$ Hz contains an inductor of inductance $25$ mH. What must be the capacitance of a capacitor connected in parallel with it for resonance to occur in the circuit ($\mu$F)?

A resistor of resistance $10~\Omega$, a capacitor of capacitance $0.5~\mu$F and an inductor of inductance $0.5$ H are connected in series to an AC generator of variable frequency. The rms voltage across the generator terminals is $140$ V. What is the rms current at resonance (A)?

An inductor of reactance $20~\Omega$, a capacitor of reactance $20~\Omega$ and a resistor of resistance $10~\Omega$ are connected in series to an AC circuit with a voltage amplitude of $300$ V. What is the current amplitude in the circuit at resonance (A)?

A resistor of resistance $3~\Omega$, an inductor of reactance $2~\Omega$ and a capacitor of reactance $6~\Omega$ are connected in series to an AC circuit. What power is dissipated in this circuit when the rms current is $2$ A (W)?
In an AC circuit, the current amplitude is $5$ A, the voltage amplitude is $200$ V and the power factor is $0.8$. Find the active power of the circuit (W).
An AC motor operates at an rms voltage of $380$ V with a power of $912$ W. If the power factor is $0.8$, find the current in its windings (A).

A circuit is made up of a resistance of $8~\Omega$, a capacitive reactance of $9~\Omega$ and an inductive reactance of $3~\Omega$ connected in series, and an AC voltage with an rms value of $140$ V is applied across it. Find the active power in the circuit (W).

An AC circuit consists of a resistor of resistance $30~\Omega$, an inductor of reactance $20~\Omega$ and a capacitor of reactance $10~\Omega$. If a current with an rms value of $2.5$ A flows through the circuit, how many joules of heat are released in it in $4$ s?

In a series AC circuit, the inductive reactance is $600~\Omega$, the resistance is $400~\Omega$ and the capacitive reactance is $300~\Omega$. If the rms current in the circuit is $2$ A, what is the power of the current (W)?
In an AC circuit, the reactance is $4~\Omega$, the resistance is $5~\Omega$, and the amplitude of the alternating current is $2\sqrt2$ A. Find the average power of the current (W).

A resistor of resistance $3~\Omega$, an inductor of reactance $2~\Omega$ and a capacitor of reactance $6~\Omega$ are connected in series to an AC circuit. If the rms current is $2$ A, find the amount of heat released in this circuit in $10$ s (J).
